label: QBO to CSV
summary: Extract transaction rows from a QBO bank feed file into a clean CSV you can inspect or edit.
detail: Read bank STMTTRN entries, preserve dates, amounts, payee descriptions and available transaction IDs. This is a read-only export; bank configuration metadata is not recreated. This reader also handles supported OFX 1.x Windows-1252 and OFX XML UTF-8/UTF-16 variants locally, warns when required references are missing, and refuses ambiguous duplicate fields or failed bank statuses. Bank-specific compatibility is not certified.
faq: Does this change the original bank file?
answer: No. Your original QBO file is read locally and never modified or uploaded.

label: QBO to Excel
summary: Turn QBO bank feed transactions into an editable Excel spreadsheet, entirely in your browser.
detail: Export a proper .xlsx workbook with date, description, signed amount and reference columns. Investment feeds and accounting splits are outside this reader's scope. This reader also handles supported OFX 1.x Windows-1252 and OFX XML UTF-8/UTF-16 variants locally, warns when required references are missing, and refuses ambiguous duplicate fields or failed bank statuses. Bank-specific compatibility is not certified. Excel date cells are real sortable dates displayed as yyyy-mm-dd (1900 date system). Signed amounts are validated to integer cents and written as numeric two-decimal cells; references including leading zeros stay text. This does not certify imports into finance software.
faq: Is the download a real Excel workbook?
answer: Yes. The application generates an .xlsx workbook locally. It is not just a CSV renamed with an Excel extension.

label: QIF to CSV
summary: Export bank-style QIF transaction records to CSV without creating an account.
detail: Read QIF D/T/P/M/N bank fields, review the result and export. QIF split categories and investment records are not reproduced. The reader rejects duplicate date, amount and payee fields, checks that optional U amounts agree with T, and warns when cleared-state, category, split or address details are omitted. Unsupported record codes are rejected rather than silently skipped. Legacy Mac-style CR-only line endings, Windows-style CRLF and LF/mixed records are supported in the local reader. Record counts and signed transaction values are never normalized or changed when reading line endings.
faq: Will unsupported QIF bank records or duplicate amount fields be silently ignored?
answer: No. Repeated D/T/P fields, mismatched U and T amounts, mixed account sections and unknown codes fail with an error. Category, split, address and cleared-state fields are warned about but are not reproduced.

label: QIF to Excel
summary: Make a readable Excel transaction sheet from a QIF bank export.
detail: Convert basic QIF transactions to four consistent spreadsheet columns. Verify dates and signed amounts in the preview before downloading. The reader rejects duplicate date, amount and payee fields, checks that optional U amounts agree with T, and warns when cleared-state, category, split or address details are omitted. Unsupported record codes are rejected rather than silently skipped. Excel date cells are real sortable dates displayed as yyyy-mm-dd (1900 date system). Signed amounts are validated to integer cents and written as numeric two-decimal cells; references including leading zeros stay text. This does not certify imports into finance software. Legacy Mac-style CR-only line endings, Windows-style CRLF and LF/mixed records are supported in the local reader. Record counts and signed transaction values are never normalized or changed when reading line endings.
faq: Will I lose split transaction detail?
answer: Yes. This release exports basic transaction rows only and clearly warns when split/category fields are encountered.

label: IIF to CSV
summary: Inspect complete, balanced IIF TRNS groups as a CSV summary; SPL accounting allocations are excluded.
detail: The reader requires !TRNS and !SPL headers and checks each TRNS/SPL/ENDTRNS group balances exactly to zero. Only TRNS summary amounts are exported, not account-level splits, ledger entries or a bank statement. Legacy Mac-style CR-only line endings, Windows-style CRLF and LF/mixed records are supported in the local reader. Record counts and signed transaction values are never normalized or changed when reading line endings.
faq: Does this validate my IIF ledger or make it ready for importing?
answer: No. It checks whether each supported transaction group balances and exports a TRNS summary. It does not audit accounts, reconstruct SPL allocations or certify QuickBooks import.

label: IIF to Excel
summary: Inspect balanced IIF TRNS summaries in Excel; every supported source transaction group is checked before export.
detail: Read complete IIF transaction groups, verify that TRNS and SPL amounts sum to zero, and export only TRNS date, amount, memo and reference. Any incomplete or unbalanced group blocks conversion. Excel date cells are real sortable dates displayed as yyyy-mm-dd (1900 date system). Signed amounts are validated to integer cents and written as numeric two-decimal cells; references including leading zeros stay text. This does not certify imports into finance software. Legacy Mac-style CR-only line endings, Windows-style CRLF and LF/mixed records are supported in the local reader. Record counts and signed transaction values are never normalized or changed when reading line endings.
faq: Are SPL allocations or a full accounting ledger included?
answer: No. Account allocations are not exported. The generated workbook is a read-only TRNS summary, not an accounting migration or QuickBooks import file.

label: OFX to CSV

label: QuickBooks CSV Formatter
summary: Map bank CSV columns, preview duplicate and formula warnings, and export a validated QuickBooks Online 3-column manual-upload CSV.
detail: Preserves exact signed cents, formats US dates and checks 1,000-row / 350 KB parts. Each part is reparsed and totals reconciled before download. Multiple parts include a privacy-minimized validation JSON. Spreadsheet-formula-like descriptions are prefixed for safety. This is not a .qbo Web Connect file and QuickBooks import has not been verified.
faq: Does it guarantee a successful QuickBooks Online import?
answer: No. It checks local CSV syntax, amount totals and file-size limits. You must review warnings, select the correct account, upload manually and verify imported transactions in QuickBooks Online.

label: CSV to QIF (Preview)
summary: Map a CSV bank transaction list and generate a basic QIF Bank file for testing.
detail: QIF Bank export is generated entirely in your browser, then re-parsed to compare every source transaction's date, signed amount, payee, reference and memo in exact order. Literal carets (^) and Unicode are preserved; newlines and control characters in QIF text fields cause a clear error instead of silently modifying the bank data. This is syntax validation only: your finance application's real import behavior is unverified.
faq: Can I convert CSV payees with line breaks or a ^ character without altering data?
answer: A literal ^ in a payee or reference is preserved. QIF uses one physical line for each field, so payees, references or memos containing newlines/control characters cannot be exported losslessly; the tool blocks that QIF download. The file is checked by reading it back locally, but compatibility with specific accounting apps remains unverified.
